 More Automation, Tighter Compliance: India’s CGST Amendment Rules 2026 Explained
 28 October 2026 
 Posted by India Briefing 
 Written by 
 Archana Rao 
 In this article 
 India’s Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Amendment Rules 2026 bring important changes to GST registration, e-commerce supplies, registration cancellation and suspension, input tax credit (ITC), and tax refund procedures. These amendments also expand system-driven compliance mechanisms and revise several GST forms.

 The Union Ministry of Finance notified the amendments through Notification No. 05/2026–Central Tax (G.S.R. 919(E)) dated 26 October 2026 . Businesses must prepare for the changes in phases, beginning 1 November 2026.
 Key Effective Dates Under the CGST Amendment Rules 2026 
 Effective date 
 Key amendments 
 1 November 2026
 New Rule 14B registration option for eligible e-commerce suppliers; revised GST cancellation procedures; changes to GST practitioner enrolment amendments
 1 December 2026
 Revised FORM GST RFD-01 and other registration- and refund-related amendments
 1 April 2027
 Revised registration suspension framework; system-based revocation of cancellation; revised ITC restriction procedures; changes to refund calculations involving capital goods
 E-commerce sellers can use an ECO warehouse for GST registration
 New Rule 14B introduces an alternative GST registration option for certain suppliers selling through an electronic commerce operator (ECO) required to collect tax at source under Section 52 of the CGST Act.
 Under this provision, a person already registered in one state or union territory can obtain GST registration in another state or union territory without maintaining a physical presence there. The supplier can declare an eligible ECO warehouse as its principal place of business in that location.
 This facility can help online sellers expand into new markets without establishing their own offices or warehouses solely for GST registration.
 Eligibility and application requirements
 Suppliers must meet three conditions to use this facility:
 They must intend to make supplies through an eligible ECO
 Their total output tax liability on the specified supplies to registered persons must not exceed INR 2,50,000 per month
 The ECO must consent to the use of its warehouse as the supplier’s principal place of business
 Eligible suppliers must apply through FORM GST REG-01 and provide the required warehouse details.
 GST registration amendments to impact businesses with multiple entries
 The amended rules revise the procedure for changing GST registration particulars and introduce deemed approval in specified circumstances.
 When a taxpayer applies to amend registration details, the authorised tax officer must act within the prescribed timeline. If the officer does not act within that period, the rules may treat the amendment as approved and make the updated registration certificate available electronically through the GST common portal.
 Certain changes to a business’s legal name or the details of its partners, directors, Karta , trustees, managing committee, CEO, or equivalent responsible persons will also apply across all GST registrations held under the same Permanent Account Number (PAN).
 Greater compliance readiness for GST cancellation applications
 From 1 November 2026, amended Rule 20 requires registered persons seeking GST cancellation to apply within 30 days of the event that warrants cancellation, except in the case of the death of a sole proprietor.
 Applicants must provide details of:
 Inputs held in stock.
 Inputs contained in semi-finished and finished goods.
 Capital goods held in stock.
 The related tax liability.
 Payments made against that liability.
 Taxpayers must also file all returns and statements due up to the cancellation date before submitting the application. If a taxpayer has filed GSTR-1 or used the Invoice Furnishing Facility for a tax period, the taxpayer must also file the corresponding GSTR-3B.
 GST registration suspension rules to tighten
 Revised Rule 21A will introduce a more system-driven process for suspending GST registrations in specified cases of non-compliance from 1 April 2027.
 The system may suspend a registration electronically if a taxpayer:
 Fails to file a composition taxpayer’s annual return for more than three months after its due date.
 Fails to file monthly returns for six consecutive months.
 Fails to file quarterly returns for two consecutive tax periods.
 Fails to comply with Rule 10A.
 GST authorities will issue an electronic notice in FORM GST REG-31, generally giving taxpayers 30 days to file outstanding returns or meet the applicable requirement.
 During suspension, taxpayers cannot make taxable supplies or issue tax invoices charging GST. If they complete the required compliance within the prescribed period, the rules deem the suspension revoked.
 System-based revocation of GST registration cancellation
 New Rule 23A introduces a system-based mechanism for revoking GST registration cancellation through the GST common portal in specified cases.
 Taxpayers whose registrations have been deemed cancelled electronically under the relevant provisions can apply for revocation through FORM GST REG-21 within 180 days of the cancellation date.
 Before applying, they must resolve the underlying compliance failure. For cancellations resulting from non-filing of returns, taxpayers must file outstanding returns and pay the applicable tax, interest, penalty, and late fee.
 Once taxpayers complete the required compliance, the system deems the revocation application approved electronically. They must then file any returns that fell due between cancellation and revocation within 30 days of the revocation order.
 Revised procedure to restrict fraudulent or ineligible ITC
 Amended Rule 86A will establish a more structured procedure for restricting the use of ITC that the authorities consider fraudulently availed or ineligible.
 An authorised tax officer can issue FORM GST DRC-26 to restrict debits of the relevant amount from a taxpayer’s electronic credit ledger.
 Authorities will maintain the restriction until the earlier of:
 One year from the date of the order.
 The date on which the proper officer permits the taxpayer to use the credit because the grounds for the restriction no longer exist.
 How taxpayers can challenge an ITC restriction
 Taxpayers can challenge a restriction by submitting an objection through FORM GST DRC-27. The authorised tax officer must provide a reasonable opportunity to be heard and issue a decision through FORM GST DRC-28. The officer may restore the taxpayer’s ability to debit the electronic credit ledger or reject the objection and maintain the restriction.
 GST refund processing will become more automated
 The amendments change refund acknowledgement timelines and provisional refund procedures to improve automation and provide greater certainty to taxpayers.
 Shorter timeline for refund acknowledgements
 Amended Rule 90 reduces the prescribed period for the relevant refund application acknowledgement or deficiency communication from 15 days to 10 days.
 If the authorities do not issue an acknowledgement in FORM GST RFD-02 or a deficiency communication in FORM GST RFD-03 within 10 days of the refund application, the rules deem the application acknowledged.
 This shorter timeline can help businesses obtain greater certainty about the status of their refund applications.
 System-based risk evaluation for provisional refunds
 Amended Rule 91 introduces a system-driven approach to provisional refunds. The GST common portal will identify and evaluate risk and generate FORM GST RFD-04 within three working days of the relevant acknowledgement.
 The system-generated order will not require revalidation by the proper officer.
 Exporters and other refund claimants should maintain accurate supporting documents and establish procedures to address discrepancies promptly.
 Change in refund calculations for inverted duty structures
 The amendments revise the formula for calculating refunds arising from an inverted duty structure, where the tax burden on inputs exceeds the GST applicable to outward supplies.
 The amended formula is as follows:
 Maximum Refund Amount = (Turnover of inverted-rated supplies × Net ITC ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover) − Tax payable on inverted-rated supplies 
 The revised definition of Net ITC includes eligible input services and ITC on capital goods attributable to the relevant period.

 Capital goods to impact certain refund calculations
 CGST rules will introduce the concept of capital goods attributable to the relevant period for specified refund calculations.
 The mechanism broadly allocates eligible ITC on capital goods over a 60-month period, subject to prescribed conditions. A specific formula determines the amount attributable to the relevant refund period.
 Businesses claiming refunds that include ITC on capital goods must maintain records demonstrating the credit’s eligibility and allocation to the relevant period.
 The amended refund documentation will also require a declaration confirming that the relevant capital goods:
 Have not been sold, disposed of, or permanently removed.
 Remain eligible for ITC.
 Are being used for the relevant zero-rated or inverted-rated supplies.
 Revised FORM GST RFD-01 from 1 December 2026
 A revised FORM GST RFD-01 will replace the existing form from December 1, 2026.
 The updated form requires information including:
 GSTIN or temporary ID
 Legal name and trade name
 Registration status
 Tax period
 Tax, interest, penalty, and fees
 Refund amount
 Grounds for claiming the refund
 Whether the claim includes ITC on capital goods
 Businesses filing refund applications from December 2026 should ensure their GST records and supporting documents contain the information required by the revised form.
 Prepare for the CGST Amendment Rules 2026
 The CGST Rules 2026 combine greater automation with stricter compliance requirements. Businesses should prioritise the following actions based on their operations and the applicable deadlines.
 E-commerce businesses
 Check eligibility for the new Rule 14B registration option
 Obtain ECO consent before using its warehouse as the principal place of business
 Monitor the applicable tax-liability threshold and maintain supporting records
 Businesses with multiple GST registrations
 Review registration details across all states and union territories
 Update legal names and responsible persons’ details consistently across registrations under the same PAN
 Track amendment applications and updated registration certificates
 Companies planning closure or restructuring
 File pending returns and statements before applying for cancellation
 Reconcile stock, semi-finished and finished goods, and capital goods
 Calculate and settle applicable tax liabilities on time
 All GST-registered businesses
 Monitor return filing, bank-account details under Rule 10A, ITC eligibility and supporting documentation, registration status and notices, and refund claims.
 Exporters and refund claimants
 Prepare for the revised FORM GST RFD-01
 Review refund calculations under the inverted duty structure provisions
 Maintain records supporting capital goods eligibility and attribution
 Update refund procedures for system-based processing
 Conclusion
 The CGST (Amendment) Rules, 2026 move GST administration towards a more automated, system-driven, and compliance-focused framework. Businesses will need to adapt their registration, return filing, ITC management, and refund procedures to the amended requirements.
 By mapping each amendment to its effective date and addressing the provisions relevant to their operations, businesses can reduce compliance gaps and minimise disruption ahead of the applicable deadlines.
